parties: Emerge Green Power Private Limited | Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (SHYAMMETL)
headline: Emerge Green Power acquires 26% stake in Shyam Metalics and Energy, becoming associate
sum: Emerge Green Power Private Limited acquired 26% stake in listed energy and metallurgical firm Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (SHYAMMETL), elevating itself to associate status. The transaction, disclosed via NSE intimation on 18 June 2026, triggers consolidated financial statement and related-party disclosure obligations under IAS 28 and Indian GAAP Schedule VI Part II.
implication: A 26% stake crossing the 'significant influence' threshold under IAS 28 requires the acquirer to account for the investee as an associate using the equity method and mandates full related-party transaction disclosures; this structuring preserves operating autonomy while locking in governance rights and consolidated reporting obligations.
detail: Emerge Green Power Private Limited has acquired 26% of the issued share capital of Shyam Metalics and Energy Limited (NSE: SHYAMMETL), a listed company engaged in metallurgical and energy operations. The stake acquisition was formally intimated to the NSE on 18 June 2026 via corporate action notification. Under Indian accounting standards (IAS 28 and GAAP Schedule VI Part II), a 26% shareholding typically confers significant influence without absolute control, requiring Emerge to consolidate SHYAMMETL as an associate in its financial statements and mandating enhanced disclosure of related-party transactions. The intimation did not disclose the acquisition price, payment terms, or specific closing conditions.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg 30 & Schedule III
framework.note: central – acquirer must disclose to stock exchange any material change in shareholding and related-party transactions within one business day

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 – Section 2(1)(za) (definition of 'associate') & Section 129 (subsidiary/associate consolidation in standalone financials)
framework.note: central – legal definition of associate; SHYAMMETL must consolidate Emerge as associated entity in its standalone balance sheet

framework.ref: Indian Accounting Standards (IAS 28) / Indian GAAP Schedule VI Part II
framework.note: central – mandates equity method accounting for associates; requires one-line consolidation in parent financials
relevant if either Emerge or SHYAMMETL promoters/directors are deemed insiders; requires pre-clearance and trading windows

framework.ref: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Reg 3(d) & Schedule I
framework.note: central if stake exceeds 25% (triggering 'acquisition' classification); may exempt if Emerge is financial investor or if SHYAMMETL board consents; opens to mandatory open offer if 26% → controlling stake path implied

framework.ref: Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014 – Rule 4 (related-party transactions)
framework.note: procedurally central – any related-party transaction between Emerge and SHYAMMETL post-acquisition requires board/shareholder approval under Rule 4

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961 – Section 56(2)(viia) (fair valuation of shares acquired above fair market value) & Section 43(5) (cost of acquisition)
framework.note: Emerge may be subject to TCS/income recognition rules if acquisition price significantly exceeds fair market value

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (if Emerge is foreign-controlled) – Schedule I & RBI Liberalized Remittance Scheme
framework.note: relevant only if Emerge is NRI/foreign entity; governs repatriation of dividends from SHYAMMETL

conditions: Acquisition resulted in Emerge Green Power becoming an 'associate' under IAS 28 / Indian GAAP Schedule VI Part II (26% stake conferring significant influence)
No conditions precedent, payment terms or post-closing milestones disclosed in NSE intimation
approvals: NSE intimation (corporate action filing) — completed 18 June 2026
SEBI substantial acquisition classification — likely triggered (≥25% stake); status of mandatory open offer exemption unclear from disclosure
structure.novel: The structuring preserves Emerge's investor status while securing associate-level governance rights; the 26% threshold is deliberately below controlling stake (50%+), minimizing triggering of full subsidiary consolidation rules and allowing SHYAMMETL to retain operational autonomy while exposing Emerge to proportionate equity-method accounting and consolidated financial statement consolidation.

triggers.law: SEBI (Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers) Regulations, 2011 – Reg 3(d)
triggers.note: A 26% acquisition is classified as a 'substantial acquisition' under Reg 3(d); may trigger mandatory open offer requirement unless exempted (e.g., financial investor, board consent, or prior shareholding exemption)

triggers.law: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 – Reg 30
triggers.note: Intimation of material change in control or 5% shareholding change must be disclosed to stock exchange within one business day; NSE filing on 18 Jun 2026 satisfies this requirement
26% stake triggers 'associate' classification; both entities must consolidate proportionately in standalone and consolidated financial statements using equity method
Significant influence (typically 20%–50% stake) mandates equity-method accounting by Emerge in its consolidated statements; SHYAMMETL's standalone statements also reflect associate status
